sourcedFrom: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: A break-open comes apart into three pieces and back together in a minute, so the job is less about disassembly than about two surfaces: the bores, and the hinge pin area where the receiver and fore-end iron carry the whole load of firing. Beretta is emphatic about the second one.

steps.title: Unloaded before anything moves
steps.action: Open the gun, look into both chambers and take out anything in them. On a break-open this is the easiest check in shooting — there is no excuse for skipping it, and Beretta puts the demand at the head of the disassembly chapter.
steps.quote: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED BEFORE BEGINNING DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURES.
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: Fore-end catch lever down, fore-end forward and off
steps.action: Pull the fore-end catch lever down and turn the fore-end forward to take it off the receiver. It comes away as one piece with its iron; nothing is under tension.
steps.aside: Pull the fore-end catch lever down
steps.quote: Turn the fore-end forward to remove it from the receiver
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Top lever right, and HOLD the barrels as they tip
steps.action: Turn the top lever to the right and tilt the barrels down, holding them firmly — without the fore-end there is nothing stopping them sliding off the hinge pins and onto the floor. Then lift them gently up and out. The top lever stays open, and that is correct.
steps.aside: Lift the barrels gently upward and out of the receiver
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: Strip without recocking, if you want the springs at rest
steps.action: Tilting the barrels down recocks the hammers automatically. If you would rather store the gun with the hammers down — snap caps, trigger pulled, hammers dropped — Beretta points you at the disassembly chapter to strip it WITHOUT recocking. ⛔ Dry firing an empty over-and-under damages the firing pins; use the snap caps.
steps.aside: The snap-caps allow the shotgun to be “dry fired”.
steps.quote: Tilting the barrels down will automatically recock the hammers.
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — USE — UNLOADING, printed p.17

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: Cotton cloth on a rod with a quality gun cleaner, bronze brush if the residue needs it — and the rod always enters at the cartridge chamber, never the muzzle. Then a clean dry cloth through to take the cleaner out, then a lightly oiled one. Running a rod in from the muzzle is how a crown gets worn on a gun that will otherwise outlive you.
steps.aside: Never apply too much oil. A build up of oil will attract dirt and this can interfere with the shotgun's operation and reliability.
steps.quote: Use a cotton cloth soaked in Beretta gun cleaner and a cleaning rod to remove firing residues from the barrels. Use a bronze brush if necessary.
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Inner face of the receiver — but keep oil OUT of the pin holes
steps.action: Clean the inner face of the receiver, especially around the firing pin holes, and oil it lightly. ⛔ Lightly is the word, and no oil goes INTO the firing pin holes: oil in there thickens, slows the pin and gives you light strikes on the coldest morning of the year.
steps.aside: Clean the inner face of the receiver (especially the area around the firing pin holes) and oil lightly
steps.quote: Do not allow oil to enter the firing pin holes
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: ⛔ The hinge pin area is the one that must not be dry
steps.action: This is the coupling that takes the load every time the gun fires, and Beretta says outright that if it is not properly oiled the parts can seize or the gun can malfunction. Clean it and lubricate it every time. Then wipe the outside down — sweat and fingerprints are what rust a shotgun in a cabinet — and put a thin film of oil over it with a soft cloth.
steps.quote: The hinge pin area is a very important coupling area. The receiver and fore-end iron are subject to very high loads and if not properly oiled, could cause seizing of parts or shotgun malfunctioning.
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Dry before it goes away, gun and case both
steps.action: Check the shotgun AND the case or slip before storage — both must be perfectly dry. A damp case will rust a gun that was put away clean, which is why Beretta names the case and not just the gun.
steps.quote: Before storing the shotgun, always check the conditions of the shotgun and case, which must be perfectly dry. Moisture and water can damage the shotgun.
steps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

deepSteps.title: Stock removal — butt plate, then the stock bolt
deepSteps.action: Beretta publishes one step past the strip: loosen the two butt-plate fastening screws and take the plate off, put the Allen key into the stock bolt and unscrew it counter-clockwise until the stock comes away from the receiver. ⛔ Grease the screws and the screwdriver tip first — a butt plate is easy to mark and the book says so.
deepSteps.quote: loosen the two fastening screws “A” and take off the butt plate “B”;
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — STOCK REMOVAL, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ And that is the end of what Beretta publishes
deepSteps.action: Past the stock there is nothing in this book for an owner. Beretta's limit is printed plainly: no repairs without sufficient experience or training, no alterations or adjustments to any part, original Beretta spare parts only, and anything the gun actually needs goes to the manufacturer or a qualified person. That is a published DON'T and this guide stops where it stops.
deepSteps.quote: Do not attempt to make repairs to your shotgun if you are not sufficiently experienced or trained. Never make alterations or adjustments to any part of the shotgun and only use original Beretta spare parts.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Over-and-Unders User Manual — MAN0022/001 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

cleaning.name: BORES
tasks: Rod always in from the CHAMBER end — never the muzzle
Gun cleaner on a cotton cloth, bronze brush only if needed
Dry cloth through to remove cleaner residue, then a light oil

cleaning.name: RECEIVER FACE
tasks: Inner face cleaned, especially round the firing pin holes
⛔ Oil lightly — and never INTO the firing pin holes

cleaning.name: HINGE PIN & FORE-END IRON
tasks: Cleaned and lubricated every time — this coupling carries the firing load
Barrel hook and fore-end iron mechanism cleaned and lightly oiled

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE & STORAGE
tasks: Dirt, sweat and fingerprints off every outer surface
Thin film of good gun oil on a soft cloth
⛔ Gun AND case perfectly dry before it is put away

reassembly: Barrels into the receiver so the receiver's hinge pins enter their slots in the barrels.
Tilt the barrels up slowly, making sure the extractor lugs enter their slots in the receiver.
Fore-end onto the barrels, pressed against them to engage the barrel hook mechanism.
⛔ The fore-end is only locked when its lever is ALIGNED IN ITS SLOT — check it.
Close the gun, work the top lever and safety, and confirm the barrels seat without force.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: close the gun and check the top lever returns toward centre, then check the fore-end is truly locked — its catch lever must be aligned in its slot, not merely close to it. Work the safety, and open and close the gun once more to confirm the barrels seat without force.
